narrative.overview:
The page is the exhibitor's workbench seen from above. The hero is the green self-healing cutting mat: a printed 1 cm grid with heavier 5 cm lines, centimetre rulers along the top and left edges in cream, and the AR photo lying on it as a taped print. Below the hero, a sheet of warm off-white paper lies on the mat, its top edge taped down with two masking strips, and everything after that point is printed on the paper in ink: type, hairline rules, a 45° and 60° guide, and white plates holding the Studio screenshots and the demo mat inside printer's crop marks. The left ruler keeps counting down the paper, now printed in ink, without a break in the count. The world is calm, exact and physical rather than glossy or techy.

There is one loud colour, borrowed from the product. Label yellow is the colour of the AR labels on the visitor's phone and in the Studio; on the page it is the strip of tape you click, the pointer ticks on the rulers, and the text selection. Type is a condensed engineering sans, the kind printed on cutting mats and rulers, for headlines and numerals, over a plain humanist sans for reading. Japanese is a first-class language on the same URL, with a heavy rounded gothic for display and the system Japanese gothic for text.

Scope: this system is the landing page at `/` (`src/components/landing/`), the legal pages at `/privacy` and `/terms` (`src/components/legal/`), and the sign-in: the signed-out Studio at `/studio` and `/login`, which render one shared page (`src/components/studio/SignInSheet.tsx`, `sign-in.module.css`, with the form in `src/app/login/LoginForm.tsx`). All of them share the landing page's root, nav, rulers, ruler cursor and fonts through `src/components/landing/`. The signed-in Studio (exhibit list and editor) and the Viewer are an older, minimal utilitarian UI this world has not reached (see Do's and Don'ts); label yellow is the only colour they already share.
keyCharacteristics: Two surfaces with two printing inks: green mat with cream lines in the hero, off-white paper with ink everywhere below it.

One set of role variables (foreground, soft foreground, print at full, major and minor strength, ruler background, focus, shadow tint) that each surface sets for itself, so a component prints correctly on whichever surface it lies on.
One loose object per mat, tilted or taped, shadowed, settling once on load: on the landing, the hero photo; on the sign-in, the paper sheet that carries the form.
On the paper, screenshots are printed flat on white plates inside crop marks: no tilt, no shadow, no tape.
Label yellow kept for what you act on: the tape, the ruler cursor, selection, and focus on the mat.
Square corners everywhere; edges are cut paper, torn tape and printed lines.
English and Japanese with equal typographic care.

rules.name: The Label Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yellow is the AR label colour and nothing else may borrow it. It marks only what responds to you: the action tape, the ruler cursor, selection, and focus on the mat. Never use it for decoration, headings, plates or a second accent.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Every line is printed at one of three strengths of its surface's ink: cream at full, 42% and 15% on the mat; ink at full, 30% and 10% on the paper. No grey, no green on the paper, no new opacities. Components take these through the surface's role variables instead of naming a colour. Text is ink, ink soft, or, inside an input only, ink placeholder.

rules.name: The Green Stays in the Hero Rule
rules.body: Mat green ends at the paper's top edge. Below it, the page is the paper sheet; nothing green is printed on it.

rules.name: The Same Care in Both Languages Rule
rules.body: On the landing page and the legal pages, every piece of copy exists in English and Japanese (the sign-in sheet is English, like the rest of the app). Japanese headings get their own smaller sizes and looser leading (about 1.16 to 1.45), M PLUS 1 at 800 with `palt`, `word-break: keep-all`, and phrase breaks marked with `<wbr>` so lines never break inside a word. Japanese body runs at line-height 1.85 with strict line breaking.

rules.name: The Condensed Means Measured Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed is for headlines, numerals and things that measure (rulers, dimension labels, step numbers, the tape). Reading text is never condensed.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: Things on the page are measured in the page's own centimetres. The rulers, the pointer readout and the hero's dimension line all read the same CSS cm (measured from a 1 cm probe), so a stated size always agrees with the rulers.

rules.name: The Unbroken Count Rule
rules.body: The left ruler runs the full height of the page with one count. On the mat it is the cream ruler on a mat-deep band; on the paper the same ruler is printed in ink on a transparent band, layered under the mat so the mat's own ruler covers its top.

rules.name: The Printed Is Flat Rule
rules.body: Only the paper's edge, the loose object on the mat (the hero print or the sign-in sheet) and the tape cast shadows, and only the shadows above. Nothing printed (text, rules, rulers, plates, the nav) is ever lifted.

rules.name: The Already There Rule
rules.body: Motion starts from a visible state and runs once. Nothing waits invisible for a scroll trigger.

dos: **Do** keep mat green to the hero: grid, cream rulers, the taped AR print and the yellow tape; start the paper sheet at its bottom edge with the contact shadow and two masking strips.
**Do** print everything below the hero on the paper in ink, and print screens on white plates with a hairline and crop marks.
**Do** colour components through the surface roles (foreground, soft, print at full, major and minor, ruler background, focus, shade) so they print correctly on mat or paper.
**Do** use label yellow only for the action tape, the ruler cursor, selection and focus on the mat.
**Do** measure in the page's own centimetres, and keep the left ruler's count unbroken from mat to paper.
**Do** write every landing and legal string in English and Japanese, and give Japanese its own sizes, leading and phrase breaks.
**Do** keep motion to the loose object's one settle (the hero print, or the sign-in sheet), from an already-visible state, with reduced motion honoured.
**Do** put a form on a loose sheet taped to the mat, printed in ink, with white plate fields and the tape as its one submit action; print errors between rules, beside what failed.
**Do** keep the legal pages printable: the print stylesheet drops the rulers, nav, contents and footer and prints the document in ink on white.
donts: **Don't** put a phone mockup in the hero or line features up as a row of icon cards; the real AR photo, screenshots and the demo mat do the showing.
**Don't** print green on the paper, or extend the mat below the hero.
**Don't** tilt, shadow or tape a plate; on the paper, screens are printed flat.
**Don't** round corners; paper, tape and rulers are square or torn.
**Don't** use yellow as a second accent, a heading colour, a plate or decoration.
**Don't** lift anything printed with a shadow, or use a shadow other than the rest, lifted, edge-contact and tape shadows.
**Don't** set reading text in Barlow Condensed, or use the ruler's 8.5 to 10px numeral size for anything a person needs to read.
**Don't** use the mono stack for anything but inline code in notes.

**Don't** treat the signed-in Studio's (exhibit list and editor) and the Viewer's older UI (system fonts, white or near-black surfaces, the blue `#1f6feb` / `#4c8dff` link accent in `src/app/globals.css` and `src/app/studio/studio.module.css`) as part of this system, and don't extend the cutting-mat world to them without a deliberate redesign; label yellow is the only colour they share today. The signed-out Studio and `/login` are in the system (see Sign-in Sheet).
